extracted.intended_audience: receiving Office officials, patent applicants and their representatives (PCT international applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and requirements governing how a PCT receiving Office (and applicants) must handle missing or erroneously filed parts, incorporation by reference, time limits, preparation and transmission of copies, checking and correction of formalities, priority claim corrections and restoration of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of missing part furnished within applicable time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant furnishes to the receiving Office, after the date on which all requirements of Article 11(1) were fulfilled but within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7, a missing part referred to in paragraph (a) so as to complete the international application, that part shall be included in the application and the receiving Office shall correct the international filing date to the date on which the receiving Office received that part, notify the applicant accordingly and proceed as provided for in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction of the international filing date to the date the missing part is received; receiving Office must notify applicant and follow Administrative Instructions for subsequent procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date when incorporation by reference applied to missing part
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, following an invitation or otherwise, a missing part is, under Rule 20.6(b), considered to have been contained in the purported international application on the date on which one or more elements referred to in Article 11(1)(iii) were first received by the receiving Office, the receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date on which all of the requirements of Article 11(1) are fulfilled and proceed as provided in Rule 20.2(b) and (c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporation by reference is found, the filing date is the date when all Article 11(1) requirements were fulfilled; follow Rule 20.2(b),(c) processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may request disregard of furnished missing part within one month
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international filing date has been corrected because a missing part was furnished, the applicant may, within one month from the date of notification, request that the missing part be disregarded; if so, the missing part is considered not furnished and the correction of the filing date is treated as not having been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be submitted to receiving Office within one month of notification; upon grant the receiving Office proceeds as provided in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of erroneously filed entire element or part (invitation options)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office finds an entire element or part has or appears to have been erroneously filed, it shall promptly invite the applicant, at the applicant's option, either (i) to correct the purported international application by furnishing the correct element or part; or (ii) to confirm that the correct element or part was incorporated by reference under Rule 4.18; and to make observations, if any, within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office must offer choice to correct by furnishing correct material or to confirm incorporation by reference; allow observations within Rule 20.7 time limit. If the time limit expires after a 12‑month priority deadline, the Office must call attention to that circumstance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and removal when correct element furnished before Article 11(1) fulfilled
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant furnishes a correct element or part on or before the date on which all Article 11(1) requirements are fulfilled but within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7, that correct element or part shall be included in the application and the erroneously filed element or part concerned shall be removed from the application; the receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date on which all Article 11(1) requirements are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Rule 20.2(b) and (c) and Administrative Instructions for subsequent processing when correct material is provided in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and filing date correction when correct element furnished after Article 11(1) but within time limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant furnishes a correct element or part after the date on which all Article 11(1) requirements were fulfilled but within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7, the correct element or part shall be included, the erroneously filed element or part removed, and the receiving Office shall correct the international filing date to the date on which it received that correct element or part, notify the applicant and proceed as provided for in the Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office must notify applicant of corrected filing date and follow Administrative Instructions for further steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect where correct element considered contained on original receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: Where, following an invitation or otherwise, a correct element or part is, under Rule 20.6(b), considered to have been contained in the purported international application on the date on which one or more elements of Article 11(1)(iii) were first received by the receiving Office, the erroneously filed element or part concerned shall remain in the application, and the receiving Office shall accord as the international filing date the date on which all Article 11(1) requirements are fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If incorporation-by-reference findings make the correct element deemed present from the earlier date, the erroneously filed element stays and the standard filing date is used; follow Rule 20.2(b),(c) and Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant may request disregard of correct element after filing date correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international filing date has been corrected under the provision for late-furnished correct elements, the applicant may within one month request that the correct element be disregarded; if so, the correct element is considered not furnished and the erroneously filed element is considered not removed and the correction is undone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be submitted within one month from notification; the receiving Office proceeds as provided in the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of incorporation by reference (what to submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may submit to the receiving Office, within the applicable time limit under Rule 20.7, a written notice confirming that an element or part is incorporated by reference under Rule 4.18, accompanied by: (i) a sheet or sheets embodying the entire element as contained in the earlier application or embodying the part; (ii) where required, a copy of the earlier application as filed; (iii) where language differs, a translation of the earlier application into the language of the international application or into both that language and the language of any required translation; and (iv) for a part of description/claims/drawings, an indication where that part is contained in the earlier application and any translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must comply with Rule 4.18 and include complete material or translations as needed to permit the receiving Office to determine whether the element/part is completely contained in the earlier application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of complete containment by receiving Office
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office finds that the requirements of Rule 4.18 and 20.6(a) have been complied with and that the element or part is completely contained in the earlier application concerned, that element or part shall be considered to have been contained in the purported international application on the date on which one or more elements referred to in Article 11(1)(iii) were first received by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful confirmation leads the receiving Office to treat the element/part as present from the earlier receipt date for filing date purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings when incorporation-confirmation or requirements not complied with
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the receiving Office finds that a requirement under Rule 4.18 or 20.6(a) has not been complied with or that the element or part is not completely contained in the earlier application, the receiving Office shall proceed as provided for in Rule 20.3(b)(i), 20.5(b), 20.5(c), 20.5 bis(b) or 20.5 bis(c), as the case may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance triggers the alternative correction/removal procedures or invitations referenced in those Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable time limit for replies/corrections under Rule 20
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicable time limit for Rules 20.3(a),(b), 20.4, 20.5(a),(b),(c), 20.5 bis(a),(b),(c), and 20.6(a) is: (i) where an invitation was sent, two months from the date of the invitation; (ii) where no such invitation was sent, two months from the date on which one or more elements referred to in Article 11(1)(iii) were first received by the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a correction/notice is received after that time limit but before the receiving Office sends the notification under Rule 20.4(i), it shall be considered to have been received within the time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑application of certain Rules when incompatible with national law
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on specified dates, particular subparagraphs of Rules 20.3, 20.5, 20.5 bis and 20.6 are not compatible with the national law applied by the receiving Office or a designated Office, the Rules concerned shall not apply to international applications filed with or in respect of that Office for as long as they continue to be incompatible, provided the Office informs the International Bureau by the stated dates; the International Bureau shall publish the information in the Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Various dated notifications (e.g., April 5, 2006; April 9, 2020; April 14, 2016) are required; non-application due to incompatibility is limited to the duration of incompatibility and must be published by the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure where element cannot be incorporated by reference due to incompatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an element or part cannot be incorporated by reference because of the operation of the incompatibility provisions, the receiving Office shall proceed as provided in the alternative correction/removal Rules (20.3(b)(i), 20.5(b), 20.5(c), 20.5 bis(b) or 20.5 bis(c)); where the receiving Office proceeds under Rule 20.5(c) or 20.5 bis(c), the applicant may proceed as provided for in Rule 20.5(e) or 20.5 bis(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The incompatibility provisions shift processing to the standard correction/removal paths and preserve applicants' right to request disregard of furnished material where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiving Office responsibility to prepare home and search copies (Rule 21.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international application is required to be filed in one copy, the receiving Office shall be responsible for preparing the home copy and the search copy required under Article 12(1). Where the international application is required to be filed in two copies, the receiving Office shall be responsible for preparing the home copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files fewer copies than required, the receiving Office must promptly prepare the missing copies and may fix and collect a fee for doing so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant request and certification of copy after 14 months
rubrics_metrics.description: After the expiration of 14 months from the priority date, the applicant may request the receiving Office to certify a copy of the international application as being identical with the international application as filed and may transmit such certified copy to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification is free of charge and may be refused only on limited grounds (copy not identical; national security; record copy already transmitted to IB and IB has informed receiving Office). If IB has not received the record copy, the certified copy received by IB shall be considered the record copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies for applicant against payment of fee (Rule 21.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Against payment of a fee, the receiving Office shall furnish to the applicant, on request, certified copies of the international application as filed and of any corrections thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office sets and collects fee for certified copies requested by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of record copy to International Bureau (Rule 22.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the determination under Article 11(1) is positive and national security does not prevent the application from being treated as such, the receiving Office shall transmit the record copy to the International Bureau promptly after receipt or, if a security check is required, as soon as necessary clearance has been obtained; in any case it shall transmit in time for it to reach the International Bureau by the expiration of the 13th month from the priority date (if mailed, mail not later than five days prior to that expiration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely transmittal is mandatory to meet the 13‑month IB receipt requirement; if IB has notification but not the record copy by 13 months, IB shall remind the receiving Office; if not in possession by 14 months, IB shall notify applicant and receiving Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit under Article 12(3) for applicant reply to IB notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit referred to in Article 12(3) shall be three months from the date of the notification sent by the International Bureau to the applicant under Rule 22.1(c) or (g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three-month period applies to the specific Article 12(3) context where IB notifies applicant about record copy receipt status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of search copy and translations (Rule 23.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where no translation is required under Rule 12.3(a), the search copy shall be transmitted by the receiving Office to the International Searching Authority at the latest on the same day as the record copy is transmitted to the International Bureau unless no search fee has been paid; where a translation is furnished under Rule 12.3, a copy of that translation and of the request shall be transmitted as the search copy unless no search fee has been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If search fee unpaid, transmission is prompt after payment; sequence listings submitted to receiving Office instead of ISA must be promptly transmitted to the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of documents relating to earlier search on applicant request (Rule 23 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall transmit to the International Searching Authority, together with the search copy, any copy related to an earlier search requested under Rule 4.12, provided the copy was submitted by the applicant with the international application, requested to be prepared/transmitted by the receiving Office, or is available to the receiving Office in acceptable form (e.g., digital library). The receiving Office shall also transmit earlier classification results if not included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office may, by notification to IB, decide not to transmit earlier search results on applicant request; optional mutatis mutandis application where priority claims are to earlier applications filed with other Offices are described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt notification of record copy by International Bureau (Rule 24.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall promptly notify the applicant, the receiving Office, and the International Searching Authority of the fact and date of receipt of the record copy; the notification shall identify the international application by number, international filing date, applicant name, and filing date of any earlier application whose priority is claimed, and shall include a list of designated Offices and, where applicable, the Contracting States designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the record copy is received after the time limit fixed in Rule 22.3, IB must promptly notify applicant, receiving Office and ISA accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification by International Searching Authority upon receipt of search copy (Rule 25.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority shall promptly notify the International Bureau, the applicant, and, unless the ISA is the same as the receiving Office, the receiving Office, of the fact and the date of receipt of the search copy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt receipt notification ensures parties are aware the search copy has been received and search processing can begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to correct under Article 14(1)(b) (Rule 26.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall issue the invitation to correct as soon as possible, preferably within one month from receipt of the international application; the invitation shall ask the applicant to furnish the required correction and give the applicant the opportunity to make observations within the time limit under Rule 26.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt issuance of invitations is expected; applicants must be given opportunity to respond within the two‑month time limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for correction after invitation (Rule 26.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for correction referred to in Rule 26.1 shall be two months from the date of the invitation; it may be extended by the receiving Office at any time before a decision is taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office has discretion to extend the two-month limit prior to taking a decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient signatures and applicant indications when multiple applicants (Rule 26.2 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Article 14(1)(a)(i), if more than one applicant, it is sufficient that the request be signed by one of them. For Article 14(1)(a)(ii), where more than one applicant, it shall be sufficient that the indications required under Rule 4.5(a)(ii) and (iii) be provided in respect of one of them who is entitled according to Rule 19.1 to file the international application with the receiving Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simplifies formal requirements in multi-applicant situations — single authorized signatory/indications suffice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking of physical requirements for publication/reproduction (Rule 26.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application is filed in a language of publication, the receiving Office shall check compliance with physical requirements in Rule 11 only to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform international publication; where filed in a language not of publication, the receiving Office shall check physical requirements only to extent necessary for satisfactory reproduction and shall check translations and drawings for compliance as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Receiving Office's checking is limited to what is necessary for publication/reproduction; it does not need to enforce all Rule 11 details beyond that.

rubrics_metrics.name: No invitation required where physical requirements complied to necessary extent (Rule 26.3 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall not be required to issue an invitation to correct a defect under Rule 11 where the physical requirements are complied with to the extent required under Rule 26.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids unnecessary invitations where minor deviations do not affect publication/reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to translate abstract/text matter of drawings (Rule 26.3 ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the abstract or text matter of the drawings is filed in a language different from the language of the description and claims, the receiving Office shall, unless a translation is otherwise required or the abstract/text matter is in the publication language, invite the applicant to furnish a translation into the language of publication. Rules 26.1, 26.2, 26.3, 26.3 bis, 26.5 and 29.1 apply mutatis mutandis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are compatibility exceptions with national law; invitation procedure mirrors other correction invitations. If request does not comply with Rule 12.1(c) the RO shall invite the applicant to file translation to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of corrections and replacement sheets (Rule 26.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A correction to the request may be stated in a letter if it can be transferred to the request without adversely affecting clarity and reproducibility; otherwise, and for corrections of any element other than the request, the applicant must submit a replacement sheet embodying the correction and a letter drawing attention to the differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters may be used only for simple transferable corrections; replacement sheets must be provided when clarity or direct reproducibility would be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision whether corrected application considered withdrawn (Rule 26.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The receiving Office shall decide whether the applicant submitted the correction within the applicable time limit under Rule 26.2, and if so, whether the corrected international application is or is not to be considered withdrawn; however, no international application shall be considered withdrawn for lack of compliance with the physical requirements of Rule 11 if it complies to the extent necessary for reasonably uniform international publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RO must assess timeliness and effect of corrections; avoid deeming applications withdrawn for minor physical defects that do not impede publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction or addition of priority claim within 16 months (Rule 26 bis.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may correct a priority claim or add a priority claim to the request by notice submitted to the receiving Office or the International Bureau within 16 months from the priority date (or 16 months from changed priority date if applicable), provided such a notice may be submitted until the expiration of four months from the international filing date. The correction may include additional indications referred to in Rule 4.10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an early publication request has been made, notices received after that request may be disregarded unless the request is withdrawn before technical preparations for publication are completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defects in priority claims and declaration of being 'considered void' (Rule 26 bis.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the receiving Office or, failing that, the International Bureau, finds that a priority claim is defective (e.g., filing date later than expiry without restoration request; non-compliance with Rule 4.10; inconsistency with priority document), they shall invite the applicant to correct. If the applicant does not correct before the time limit under Rule 26 bis.1(a), that priority claim shall, subject to exceptions, be considered not to have been made ('considered void') and a declaration will be made and applicant informed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions where a claim is not considered void are limited (missing number, minor inconsistencies, or filing date within two months). IB will publish information on such priority claims and any applicant-submitted information received before completion of technical preparations for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication option after expiry of priority-correction time limit (Rule 26 bis.1(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant wishes to correct or add a priority claim after the time limit has expired, the applicant may (before expiration of 30 months from the priority date and subject to payment of a special fee fixed in the Administrative Instructions) request the International Bureau to publish information concerning the matter; the IB shall promptly publish such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late corrections can be made public upon payment of a special fee, subject to time constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of right of priority by receiving Office (Rule 26 bis.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the international filing date is later than the priority period expiry but within two months from that date, the receiving Office shall, on request and subject to specified paragraphs, restore the right of priority if it finds that a criterion applied by it is satisfied, namely (i) failure occurred in spite of due care required by the circumstances having been taken, or (ii) failure was unintentional. Each receiving Office shall apply at least one criterion and may apply both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request must be filed within the applicable time limit (two months from expiry), state reasons, preferably include declaration/evidence, and may require adding a missing priority claim; the RO may charge a fee, may require evidence, shall give opportunity to make observations before refusing, and must promptly notify IB of receipt, decision, and the criterion relied upon.
